description: Crescent Heights has filed plans for a 43-story, approximately 557-foot mixed-use tower at 1575 Alton Road in Miami Beach's Flamingo / Lummus neighborhood, east of West Avenue on the site of a 1935 Firestone building later converted to restaurant use. RSP Architects designed a slender tower rising from a multi-story podium with white and brown-toned facades, floor-to-ceiling glazing, projecting balconies, and a perforated screen concealing structured parking. The Live Local Act filing calls for 163 residences, including 62 workforce units on the lower floors (households up to 120% AMI) and about 101 market-rate residences from roughly the 15th floor through level 43. Floridian Development has described those upper homes as likely for-sale condominiums; the same outlet's project record lists the usage as multifamily, and Crescent Heights has not confirmed a sales program. Filed program elements include about 4,107 square feet of indoor amenity space, a swimming pool, outdoor terraces, resident club areas, 1,739 square feet of Alton Road retail, and 149 parking spaces. The proposal is under administrative review and has not been approved. Pricing, floor plans, and a sales or lease timeline have not been released.
editorialLine: Crescent Heights filed under the Live Local Act, which lets the tower rise past the height Miami Beach zoning allows.

faq.question: What is proposed at 1575 Alton Road in Miami Beach?
faq.answer: Crescent Heights has filed plans for a 43-story, approximately 557-foot mixed-use tower with 163 residences on the east side of Alton Road between 15th Terrace and 16th Street, in the Flamingo / Lummus neighborhood. The filing includes 62 workforce units on the lower floors, about 101 market-rate residences from roughly the 15th floor through level 43, about 1,739 square feet of ground-floor retail, and 149 parking spaces. As of September 2026 it is under administrative review and has not been approved.

faq.question: Will 1575 Alton Road be condos or rentals?
faq.answer: Not confirmed. Floridian Development has described the larger upper-floor residences as likely intended as for-sale condos, while its project profile lists the usage as multifamily. The 62 workforce units on the lower floors carry rents restricted to households earning up to 120% of area median income. Crescent Heights has not confirmed a sales program, pricing, or floor plans.

faq.question: How tall will the 1575 Alton Road tower be?
faq.answer: Trade coverage of the filing calls for 43 stories at approximately 557 feet, two feet below the 559-foot Blue and Green Diamond towers on Collins Avenue, which completed in 2000. At that height it would rank just below the Diamond pair among Miami Beach's tallest buildings.

faq.question: Who is the developer and architect?
faq.answer: The developer is Crescent Heights, filing through the entity ARRP Miami IV, LLC. RSP Architects designed the tower, a slender residential shaft rising from a multi-story podium with a screened parking garage along Alton Road.

faq.question: Why is 1575 Alton Road using the Live Local Act?
faq.answer: Florida's Live Local Act allows projects that include qualifying workforce housing to seek greater height and density through administrative, staff-level approval rather than the City of Miami Beach's traditional public board process. An earlier plan for the same site called for an 18-story, roughly 225-foot tower with 92 residences, 37 of them workforce units.

faq.question: What is on the site now?
faq.answer: The site holds a Firestone tire service building dating to 1935 that has since been converted to restaurant use. Trade coverage notes it is not a protected historic landmark. The filed plans would replace it with the new tower and a small retail frontage on Alton Road.

faq.question: When will pricing and floor plans be released?
faq.answer: No pricing, floor plans, or sales or lease timeline has been announced, and the project still needs approval.
